title: Players are Visible in Server Ping
description: Whether the player count and possibly a player preview will be displayed by the specified server ping. If this is false, instead of a player count and possibly a player preview, the specified server ping will display "???" where the player count should be.

title: Put JSON in List Variable
description: Puts all of the information stored inside the specified jsonobject into the specified list variable. This is needed as storing json data in list variables is currently the only way to manipulate information in ThatPacketAddon's jsonobjects other than raw string manipulation.
syntax_pattern:
put json %jsonobject% in listvar %objects%
put jsons %jsonobjects% in listvar %objects%

title: Receive Packet
description: Makes the server simulate receiving the specified packet(s) from the specified player(s)

title: Send Packet
description: Sends the specified packet(s) to the specified player(s).

title: Game Profile of Player
description: An expression for the game profile corresponding to the specified profile.

title: New Game Profile
description: An expression for a game profile with the specified name and optionally the specified UUID and skin. If the UUID is not specified a random UUID will be created and used. If the skin is not specified the profile will not have a skin associated with it.

title: Name of Game Profile
description: An expression for the name of the specified profile.

title: Skin of Game Profile
description: An expression for the skin of the specified profile.

title: UUID of Game Profile
description: An expression for the UUID of the specified profile.

title: JSON from List Variable
description: An expression for a jsonobject constructed from the information stored inside the specified list variable.

title: Legacy Enum Field of Packet
description: An expression for an enum field of a packet (first see the Packet Info o expression for a more general explanation of packet fields). The specified string is the name of the enum you are getting/setting. Using arbitrary gives you access to all enum fields, rather than just one particular type, and allows you to access certain enums that are NMS types rather than ProtocolLib and thus can't be accessed by their name.

title: Legacy Field of Packet
description: An expression for the packet field of either the specified type or referred to by the specified string, with the specified index, of the specified packet. For example, 'string' can be used as the specified type to get a string field in the specified packet. 'array' must be included in the syntax when the fields are plural (ex. 'string array'). Use 'object' in order to access all fields of the packet. However, some fields will have objects in raw forms that cannot be easily used in Skript without the use of addons such as skript-mirror. Many of these fields can be converted into Skript types; most of these fields must be referred to by a certain string rather than a type: "uuid", "material", "blockdata", "collection" array, "bytebuffer" array (The last two are plural and must have array included in the syntax.

title: Legacy JSON Field of Packet
description: An expression for certain fields of packets (first see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation) that don't have equivalent types in Skript, and thus must be represented in the form of a jsonobject. The names of the fields can be written as strings but don't have to be. Current accept JSON infos: 'chatcomponent', 'serverping', 'datawatcher', 'watchablecollection', 'gameprofile', 'nbt', 'chatcomponent' array, 'playerinfodata' array.

title: Legacy Number Array Field of Packet
description: An expression for int array and byte array fields of packets. First see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation of packet fields.

title: Legacy Number Field of Packet
description: An expression for different kinds of number fields of packets. First see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation of packet fields.

title: Key of Minecraft Key
description: An expression for the key string of the specified minecraft key.

title: Prefix of Minecraft Key
description: An expression for the prefix of the specified minecraft key.
syntax_pattern:

title: NBT List Field of Packet
description:
The value of the field numbered at the specified index of the specified packet's NBT list fields. The NBT values contained int list, as well as any NBT values contained in those NBT values, are represented as a jsonobject with three parts:
The name, with index/key "name", which is just the name (sometimes null)
The type, with index/key "type", which is the type of NBT, and can have the following values:
- "byte", "short", "int", "long", "float", "double", the basic number types
- "string", for strings
- "byte_array" and "int_array", for basic number array types
- "compound", for an NBT compound
- "list_something", such as "list_string" or "list_compound", for a list of some other type
The value, with index/key "value", which is the actual value:
- In the cases of the number types and string type this is just the number/string (when accessing using a list variable in Skript it's like {_nbt::value}
- In the case of the number array types and the list type this is an array of the objects (when accessing using a list variable in Skript it's like {_nbt::value::*}, ex. {_nbt::value::1} for the first element)
- In the case of the compound it's a JSONObject of the NBT values, each also having its own name, type and value (when accessing through a list variable in Skript it's: {_nbt::value::example_name::name} for the name (which is the same as the index, so it will be "example_name"), {_nbt::value::example_name::type} for the type, let's say "string", and {_nbt::value::example_name::value} for the actual value, let's say "pie") The index defaults to 0 if unspecified and the packet expression defaults to event-packet if unspecified.

title: Display Name of PlayerInfoData

The name of the game profile contained in the specified playerinfodata is only used internally.

title: Gamemode of PlayerInfoData
description: An expression for the gamemode contained in the specified playerinfodata. Note that ProtocolLib's NativeGameMode class also has a NOT_SET mode, which will appear in Skript as the expression being not set.

title: Game Profile of PlayerInfoData
description: The profile contained in this playerinfodata. Determines the skin that will be displayed as an icon if this playerinfodata is used as a tab in the tablist.

title: Latency of PlayerInfoData
description:
The latency contained in this playerinfodata, respresented as an integer amount of milliseconds. Different values of latency will result in different latency bar icons being displayed if the specified playerinfodata is used as a tab in the tablist:
latency < 0 ms will show a red X
0 ms <= latency < 150 ms will show 5 bars
150 ms <= latency < 300 ms will show 4 bars
300 ms <= latency < 600 ms will show 3 bars
600 ms <= latency < 1000 ms = 1 second will show 2 bars
1000 ms = 1 second <= latency will show 1 bar

title: New PlayerInfoData
description: An expression for a new playerinfodata with the specified profile and display name, either the specified latency or 0 if the latency is not specified, and either the specified gamemode or the NOT_SET gamemode if the gamemode is not specified.

title: MOTD of Server Ping
description: An expression for the MOTD (message of the day) that the specified server ping will display.

title: New Server Ping
description: An expression for a new server ping.

title: Players Online or Max Players of Server Ping
description: An expression for either the amount of players online or the player limit displayed by the specified server ping. You can pretty much set these to be whatever you want, they can even be negative.
syntax_pattern:
players online (of|in) [server] ping %serverping%
[server] ping %serverping%'s players online
max players (of|in) [server] ping %serverping%
[server] ping %serverping%'s max players

title: Player Preview of Server Ping
description: A list expression of game profiles whose names will be displayed by the specified server ping as a preview of the players on your server. As with other parts of the server ping, these profiles don't actually have to be in any way related to the players actually online on your server.
syntax_pattern:
player preview of [server] ping %serverping%
[server] ping %serverping%'s player preview

title: Version Name of Server Ping
description: An expression for the string that will be displayed by the specified server ping as the version of your server if the client is not compatible with your server. This version name is not actually used for checking version compatibility; instead, the Version Protocol of Server Ping expression is used.

title: Packet Field Alias
description: Not an actual event, but rather a group of packet field aliases to be used with packets of the specified packettype. Packet info aliases are aliases for specific usages of packet info expressions. Under the main scope lines are written in the form '<new syntax> = <old syntax>', where the old syntax is how you would normally write an expression for the desired packet info, and the new syntax is how you want to be able to write it. Note that the new syntax is essentially being registered as a Skript syntax, so you can write it with features of Skript syntax like optional parts enclosed in '[]', and multiple usages of '%packet%' are allowed in your syntax, though only one of them should be possible to use at a time since only one packet is used to evaluate the alias Your syntax does not have to require or even allow the usage of '%packet%'. In this case, 'event-packet' will be used as the packet. A small addition to normal Skript syntax is that now, if you would like to have a group of different options for syntax but also have the whole thing be optional, instead of writing '[(a|b|...)]' you can write '[a|b|...]'.

title: Packet Event
description: Called when a packet of one of the specified types is being sent or received. You can optionally specify a priority; triggers with higher priority will be called later (so high priority will come after low priority, and monitor priority will come last). By default, the priority is normal.

title: Game Profile
description: A game profile is meant to represent the profile of a player, and contains a name, UUID, and skin.

title: JSONObject

Useful in Skript for transmitting complex information that isn't represented by a type in cases where list variables can't be used (ex. returning values from expressions/functions (ex. the JSON Field of Packet expression)).

title: Minecraft Key
description: A type of key used by Minecraft in packets consisting of a prefix and a key string.

title: Packet
description: A packet. Packets are used by the Minecraft client and server to transmit information, and can be intercepted, read, and modified in order to gain information and modify the behavior of your server in certain ways that are not possible through Bukkit.

title: PlayerInfoData
description: A type describing a tab in the tablist, usually describing a player.

title: Server Ping

The index defaults to 0 if unspecified and the packet expression defaults to event-packet if unspecified.

title: NBT Field of Packet
description:
The value of the field numbered at the specified index of the specified packet's NBT fields. The NBT, as well as any NBT values contained in it, is represented as a jsonobject with three parts:
The name, with index/key "name", which is just the name (sometimes null)
The type, with index/key "type", which is the type of NBT, and can have the following values:
- "byte", "short", "int", "long", "float", "double", the basic number types
- "string", for strings
- "byte_array" and "int_array", for basic number array types
- "compound", for an NBT compound
- "list_something", such as "list_string" or "list_compound", for a list of some other type
The value, with index/key "value", which is the actual value:
- In the cases of the number types and string type this is just the number/string (when accessing using a list variable in Skript it's like {_nbt::value}
- In the case of the number array types and the list type this is an array of the objects (when accessing using a list variable in Skript it's like {_nbt::value::*}, ex. {_nbt::value::1} for the first element)
- In the case of the compound it's a JSONObject of the NBT values, each also having its own name, type and value (when accessing through a list variable in Skript it's: {_nbt::value::example_name::name} for the name (which is the same as the index, so it will be "example_name"), {_nbt::value::example_name::type} for the type, let's say "string", and {_nbt::value::example_name::value} for the actual value, let's say "pie") The index defaults to 0 if unspecified and the packet expression defaults to event-packet if unspecified.

title: Particle Field of Packet
description: The value of the field numbered at the specified index of the specified packet's particle fields. This is an automatically generated enum packet field, and is represented in Skript as a string (the name of the value of the field). The returned name will always be in uppercase, however when setting this expression the cases used do not matter.The different values of this enum are "EXPLOSION_NORMAL", "EXPLOSION_LARGE", "EXPLOSION_HUGE", "FIREWORKS_SPARK", "WATER_BUBBLE", "WATER_SPLASH", "WATER_WAKE", "SUSPENDED", "SUSPENDED_DEPTH", "CRIT", "CRIT_MAGIC", "SMOKE_NORMAL", "SMOKE_LARGE", "SPELL", "SPELL_INSTANT", "SPELL_MOB", "SPELL_MOB_AMBIENT", "SPELL_WITCH", "DRIP_WATER", "DRIP_LAVA", "VILLAGER_ANGRY", "VILLAGER_HAPPY", "TOWN_AURA", "NOTE", "PORTAL", "ENCHANTMENT_TABLE", "FLAME", "LAVA", "FOOTSTEP", "CLOUD", "REDSTONE", "SNOWBALL", "SNOW_SHOVEL", "SLIME", "HEART", "BARRIER", "ITEM_CRACK", "BLOCK_CRACK", "BLOCK_DUST", "WATER_DROP", "ITEM_TAKE", "MOB_APPEARANCE", "DRAGON_BREATH", "END_ROD", "DAMAGE_INDICATOR", "SWEEP_ATTACK", "FALLING_DUST", "TOTEM", "SPIT". The index defaults to 0 if unspecified and the packet expression defaults to event-packet if unspecified.

title: TitleAction Field of Packet
description: The value of the field numbered at the specified index of the specified packet's titleaction fields. This is an automatically generated enum packet field, and is represented in Skript as a string (the name of the value of the field). The returned name will always be in uppercase, however when setting this expression the cases used do not matter.The different values of this enum are "TITLE", "SUBTITLE", "ACTIONBAR", "TIMES", "CLEAR", "RESET". The index defaults to 0 if unspecified and the packet expression defaults to event-packet if unspecified.

title: Version Protocol of Server Ping
description: An expression for the version protocol specified by the specified server ping. This is used to check whether the client is compatible with your server.
syntax_pattern:
version protocol of [server] ping %serverping%
[server] ping %serverping%'s version protocol

title: PacketType
description: A type of a packet. The ones that are available for you depend on your Minecraft version. If you would like to see them, do '/mundosk doc packettype' in your console. Alternatively, use the All Packettypes expression, loop through it, and print them.
